+# Manage AOSP Referenced Apps in Microsoft Intune - Microsoft Intune | Microsoft Learn
+
+AOSP referenced apps identify apps by package name instead of an uploaded APK. You can use Microsoft Intune to manage OEM, preloaded, or externally deployed apps on Android Open Source Project (AOSP) devices. The app must already be on the device or be deployed outside Intune.
+
+To unhide an existing app on the device, assign the referenced app as **Required**. To hide the app without deleting it, assign it as **Uninstall**. The **Available** assignment type isn't supported for referenced apps.
+
+AOSP referenced apps support user-associated and userless AOSP devices.
+
+## Before you start
+
+- Make sure the devices are enrolled in Intune with AOSP user-associated or AOSP userless enrollment.
+- Make sure the app is already on the devices, or arrange to deploy it outside Intune.
+- Get the app's package name. If you don't know the package name, contact the device manufacturer or app vendor.
+- Make sure you have permissions to create and assign apps in the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431). For permission guidance, see [Role-based access control](../../fundamentals/role-based-access-control/overview).
+
+## Select the app type
+
+Select the AOSP referenced app type to open the app creation steps. You don't need to upload an APK or select an app from Google Play.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431).
+2. Select **Apps** > **All apps** > **Create**.
+3. For **Platform**, select **Android**.
+4. For **Category**, select **Referenced apps**.
+5. Select **AOSP referenced app**, and then select **Create**.
+
+## Set app information
+
+Enter the app details and the package name that Intune uses to identify the app on the device.
+
+1. On the **App information**page, add the following details:
+    - **Name**: Enter the name of the app as it appears in Intune.
+    - **Publisher**: Enter the name of the app publisher.
+    - **Package name**: Enter the package name of the app. Intune validates that the package name is valid.
+2. Select **Next** to display the **Scope tags** page.
+
+The package name can't be changed after you create the app. To manage a different package, create a new referenced app. If you don't know the package name, contact the device manufacturer or app vendor.
+
+You can't create referenced apps for Company Portal (`com.microsoft.windowsintune.companyportal`) or Microsoft Authenticator (`com.azure.authenticator`).
+
+## Select scope tags (optional)
+
+Use scope tags to control which administrators can access the app in Intune. For more information, see [Use role-based access control and scope tags](../../fundamentals/role-based-access-control/scope-tags).
+
+1. Select **Select scope tags** to add scope tags for the app, if needed.
+2. Select **Next** to display the **Assignments** page.
+
+## Assign the app
+
+Choose group assignments to unhide or hide the app on targeted devices. AOSP referenced apps support **Required** and **Uninstall** assignments only.
+
+- **Required**: Unhides an existing, enabled app when needed. If a preinstalled system package is retained on the device but isn't installed for the current user, Intune can restore it for that user. Intune doesn't download a new APK. If the package isn't on the device, the assignment fails.
+- **Uninstall**: Hides the app without removing its APK or app data, and without disabling it. If the app is absent or already hidden, the assignment is satisfied without further action.
+
+Note
+
+An app's hidden state is separate from its enabled state. Intune can unhide or restore an app, but it can't override a disabled state set by the user, device manufacturer, or another mechanism. A **Required** assignment fails until the app is enabled outside Intune.
+
+1. Select the group assignments under **Required** or **Uninstall**.
+2. Select **Next** to display the **Review + create** page.
+
+Note
+
+If an app doesn't have a launchable activity, its icon won't appear on the home screen, even when a **Required** assignment succeeds.
+
+For group assignment guidance, see [Assign apps to groups](../deployment/assign-groups).
+
+## Review and create the app
+
+Review the app details before adding the referenced app to Intune.
+
+1. Review the values and settings on the **Review + create** page.
+2. Select **Create** to add the app to Intune.
+
+The app's **Overview** page is displayed. The referenced app also appears in the apps list.
+
+## Hide an existing referenced app
+
+To hide an OEM, preloaded, or externally deployed app, assign the referenced app as **Uninstall**. The app's APK and data remain on the device.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431).
+2. Select **Apps** > **All apps**.
+3. Select the AOSP referenced app from the apps list.
+4. Select **Properties**, and edit **Assignments**.
+5. Add the target group under **Uninstall** and remove its **Required** assignment, if one exists.
+6. Review and save the assignments.
+
+If another referenced-app **Required** assignment targets the same package on the device, it takes precedence over **Uninstall**. Removing a Required assignment alone doesn't hide the app.

+## VPN tunnel routing
+
+Microsoft Intune supports Apple’s **Enforce Routes** capability in iOS/iPadOS and macOS VPN profiles. This enhancement helps administrators mitigate traffic bypass scenarios (such as de-cloaking risks) by ensuring VPN routing behavior aligns with Apple’s platform semantics.
+
+This feature introduces a simplified configuration experience in the Intune admin center, where routing behavior is defined using **Include all networks** and **Exclude local networks** settings. Intune automatically derives the appropriate **Enforce Routes** configuration based on these selections to ensure consistent and predictable device behavior.
+
+With this update:
+
+- Intune supports Apple’s `enforceRoutes` capability for iOS/iPadOS and macOS VPN configurations.
+- Routing behavior is explicitly modeled using:
+
+    - **Include all networks**
+    - **Exclude local networks**
+- Intune automatically derives the correct `enforceRoutes` value based on the selected combination—removing the need for manual configuration.
+
+This feature helps ensure that VPN routing behavior:
+
+- Prevents unintended traffic leakage outside the VPN tunnel
+- Aligns with Apple’s NetworkExtension routing model
+- Provides consistent enforcement of routing policies across devices
+
+In particular, enabling enforcement when required ensures that traffic does not bypass VPN routing due to local route precedence, which can otherwise lead to exposure of sensitive traffic.
+
+**How routing behavior works**
+
+Apple’s VPN model defines routing behavior using a combination of:
+
+- Full tunnel behavior (**Include all networks**)
+- Local network exceptions (**Exclude local networks**)
+- Route precedence enforcement (**Enforce Routes**)
+
+Intune simplifies this model by automatically deriving `enforceRoutes` when needed.
+
+**Configuration and behavior**
+
+| Include all networks | Exclude local networks | Enforce routes (derived) | Resulting device behavior |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Off | Off | Off | Standard VPN routing based on configured routes |
+| On | Off | Ignored | Most device traffic is routed through the VPN tunnel |
+| On | On | Ignored | Most traffic is routed through the VPN, except local network traffic (for example, AirDrop, printers) |
+| Off | On | On (auto-derived) | VPN routing is enforced, and local network traffic is excluded from the tunnel |
+
+**Key behavior notes**
+
+- When **Include all networks** is enabled, iOS routes most traffic through the VPN tunnel. In this scenario, Apple ignores the `enforceRoutes` setting.
+- When **Exclude local networks** is enabled without **Include all networks**, Intune automatically enables **Enforce Routes** to ensure local network exclusions take effect.
+- **Enforce Routes is only applied when required** and isn’t exposed as a standalone setting in the admin experience.
+- These settings apply only to **device-wide VPN (tunnel routing)** configurations and aren’t applicable to **per-app VPN**.
+- Using **split tunneling** together with **VPN tunnel routing** settings is not recommended. When **split tunneling** is enabled, it forces all traffic through the VPN at the system level and may override your configured routes.
+
+**Security considerations**
+
+By enforcing routing precedence when required:
+
+- VPN traffic adheres to the configured routing policy
+- Local device routes can’t override VPN-defined routing unexpectedly
+- The risk of traffic bypass (including de-cloaking scenarios) is reduced
+
+In practice:
+
+- Use **Include all networks** to enforce a full-tunnel VPN configuration.
+- Use **Exclude local networks** only when local network access (such as printers or AirPlay) is required.
+- Avoid relying on explicit route configurations unless required by your VPN provider.
+
 ::: zone pivot="ios-ipados"

+| **Action required** | Certification authority connectivity | The connector can't reach the certification authority (CA). Confirm that the CA service is running, the connector host can reach the CA over the network, and firewall rules don't block RPC traffic. |
+| **Action required** | Connector is disconnected | The connector isn't connected to Intune. Confirm that the connector services are running on the server and that firewall rules don't block the required HTTPS connections. For more information, see [Network endpoints for Microsoft Intune](../../endpoints). |
+| **Action required** | Certification authority issuing permission | The connector service account doesn't have the permissions required to issue certificates. Review the [certificate connector service account](prerequisites#certificate-connector-service-account) and certificate template requirements in the [connector prerequisites](prerequisites). |
+| **Action required** | Certificate template configuration | The CA rejected the request. Confirm that the Intune certificate profile matches the certificate template on the CA. This condition applies to PKCS profiles. For more information, see [Configure certificate templates on the CA](../../../device-configuration/certificates/pkcs-profiles#configure-certificate-templates-on-the-ca). |
+| **Warning** | Certification authority revocation permission | The connector service account can't revoke certificates. Grant the account the **Issue and Manage Certificates** permission on the CA. For more information, see [Certificate connector service account](prerequisites#certificate-connector-service-account). |
+| **Warning** | Certificate connector connectivity | The connector intermittently loses its connection to the CA, which can delay or prevent certificate requests. Confirm that the CA service is running, the connector host can reach the CA over the network, and firewall rules don't block RPC traffic. |
+
+For more help investigating connector failures, see [Troubleshoot the Certificate Connector for Microsoft Intune](/en-us/troubleshoot/mem/intune/troubleshoot-certificate-connector-events?context=/intune/context). For information about version support and deprecated connectors, see Lifecycle.

 ## Device configuration
 
+### Maintenance windows for updates on Windows devices
+
+Microsoft Intune will introduce maintenance windows to help you schedule firmware, driver, and operating system updates on Windows devices. You'll be able to choose supported update operations and configure a start date, start time, duration, and repeat schedule.
+
+You'll create a maintenance windows profile in the Microsoft Intune admin center to define when update activity should take place. Scheduling options will include daily, weekly, and monthly recurrence, so you can align update activity with your organization's planned maintenance periods. This initial release will focus on updates; it won't include maintenance windows for application installations.
+
+Applies to:
+
+- Windows
+
+### Automate tasks with local actions on Android Enterprise devices
+
+Microsoft Intune will introduce local actions for Android Enterprise fully managed and dedicated devices. With local actions, you'll be able to automate tasks directly on a device by configuring actions that run in response to supported events. Events will include device restart, Managed Home Screen sign-in or sign-out, power connection changes, and scheduled times. Actions will include launching an app activity, sending a broadcast intent, signing out of Managed Home Screen, and exiting kiosk mode. You'll be able to pair supported events and actions, with up to five actions for each event.
+
+Applies to:
+
+- Android Enterprise fully managed devices
+- Android Enterprise dedicated devices
+
+### View eSIM profiles and deployment status for Windows devices
+
+Microsoft Intune will add Windows eSIM profile information and deployment status to the Properties Catalog. This visibility will make it easier to identify devices that require follow-up and validate profile deployment across your managed Windows estate.
+
+Applies to:
+
+- Windows
+
+### Support for the KEYENCE OEMConfig app on Android Enterprise
+
+Microsoft Intune will add support for the KEYENCE OEMConfig app (`com.keyence.autoid.oemconfigs`) for Android Enterprise devices. You'll be able to use the app with Intune's OEMConfig workflow to configure the device settings that KEYENCE exposes through its app schema.
+
+The app will be included in Intune's supported OEMConfig apps list. This addition will extend OEM-specific configuration support for organizations that use compatible KEYENCE devices. The settings available to configure will depend on the schema provided by KEYENCE, rather than a new set of Intune-defined settings.
+
+Applies to:
+
+- Android Enterprise
+

 Microsoft Intune will add Apple OS 27 declarative device management (DDM) status data to device inventory. You'll be able to review system health information for supported hardware components, content cache details, and MDM state such as enrollment type, awaiting configuration, Return to Service, Shared iPad, and Lockdown Mode. +### Controlled Configuration for Microsoft Defender Antivirus on Windows
+
+Intune will support Controlled Configuration for Microsoft Defender Antivirus settings on Windows. When you enable it, antivirus settings delivered by Intune or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint security settings management will take precedence over conflicting settings from Group Policy, Configuration Manager, and local changes or scripts. You'll be able to protect administrator-defined antivirus settings from being overridden, rather than protecting only secure default values. This will help reduce configuration drift, maintain consistent device states, and simplify troubleshooting by making the cloud-delivered configuration authoritative.

+### STIG audit baselines for Windows devices in commercial tenants
+
+Intune will support STIG audit baselines for Windows devices in commercial tenants. The baseline will evaluate supported automated checks without changing device settings, helping you understand where follow-up is needed before making configuration changes. +Helpdesk agents will be able to request device diagnostics during an attended Remote Help session on Windows.
